paragraphs: Friend, here's the heavy truth of this chapter. Solomon's throne wasn't built on his own cleverness. He says it himself: the LORD is "the One who established me, who set me on the throne of my father David, and who founded for me a dynasty as He promised" (1 Kings 2:24). The chapter closes with "Thus the kingdom was firmly established in the hand of Solomon" (1 Kings 2:46), and a promise God made is what holds it up.

Now look at the three men who ran into Solomon's king-sized judgment. Adonijah asked for something that cost him his life, and Joab ran to the altar, but Solomon said the blood Joab shed would come back on his own head (1 Kings 2:32). Shimei is the one who shows us the lesson: he said "The sentence is fair" (1 Kings 2:38) and then crossed the line he'd sworn not to cross. Saying the right words isn't the same as living them out, and I get nervous just thinking about it, because I've said "I'll be right there" to a hot oven timer and meant it less than I should have.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery today, baker. God keeps His promises, and Solomon's throne rests on what He promised. Our job is to honor what we say before Him, because words and oaths are not decoration. And this story isn't over, because Solomon's kingdom is only just getting started, so keep your apron on.
